text:
Plan: x streamwise, y lateral, z spanwise (wing mounted on the z=0 wall, tip at z=0.2). NACA 2412 sections lofted root→tip, leading edge unswept (LE at x=0 both sections), no twist. First get the profile points right and look at them.

```python
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, os
os.makedirs("constant/triSurface", exist_ok=True)

def naca2412(n=80):
    m, p, t = 0.02, 0.40, 0.12
    beta = np.linspace(0, np.pi, n)
    x = (1 - np.cos(beta)) / 2
    yt = 5*t*(0.2969*np.sqrt(x) - 0.1260*x - 0.3516*x**2 + 0.2843*x**3 - 0.1036*x**4)
    yc = np.where(x < p, m/p**2*(2*p*x - x**2), m/(1-p)**2*((1-2*p) + 2*p*x - x**2))
    dyc = np.where(x < p, 2*m/p**2*(p - x), 2*m/(1-p)**2*(p - x))
    th = np.arctan(dyc)
    xu, yu = x - yt*np.sin(th), yc + yt*np.cos(th)
    xl, yl = x + yt*np.sin(th), yc - yt*np.cos(th)
    # upper TE->LE then lower LE->TE, closed loop
    px = np.concatenate([xu[::-1], xl[1:]])
    py = np.concatenate([yu[::-1], yl[1:]])
    return px, py

px, py = naca2412()
print(len(px), px[0], py[0], px[-1], py[-1], "max t/c:", (py.max()-py.min()))
plt.figure(figsize=(8,2)); plt.plot(px, py, '-o', ms=2); plt.axis('equal'); plt.grid(True); plt.show()
```
Profile is clean and closed at the TE. Now the solid: loft root (c=0.12, z=0) to tip (c=0.08, z=0.2), LE unswept at x=0, extended below the wall plane so the boolean with the domain box is clean.
Volume check: sectional area coefficient implied is 0.0818·c², matching NACA 2412 (~0.082). Now the domain box and the fluid volume.
Volume removed (1.657e-4) equals the wing above z=0 exactly. Now group the fluid's faces into the five patches by which domain plane they lie in; everything else is wing surface.
All five patch areas match analytically. Export one STL per patch (metres, no scaling needed).
Wing STL is open only along its root curve — closed by root.stl in the union. Now a coarse background block (0.04 m cells, ~10k) with the box patches named at creation.
Now snappy: feature extraction on the wing, refinement levels (3–4) plus a near-field box, castellate+snap.
Meshed to 41.6k cells with no quality errors. Check patch areas and look at the wing surface in the mesh.
Volume matches the CAD fluid to 1e-6. Now look at it: render the wing patch and root plane.
Shape is right. Refine one level on the wing (surface 4–5, features 5) and re-check.
Right — the previous `-overwrite` replaced the background mesh; snappy must start from blockMesh again.
69.6k cells, no errors. Now measure the snapped wing geometry itself: chord at root/mid/tip and max thickness ratio.
All dimensions match. Final visual check plus a weld test of the five STLs (they should form one closed fluid boundary).
Slice looks right (cambered section, graded refinement). Redo the weld test without brace expansion.

The five patch STLs weld into one closed fluid boundary. Done.

**Built:** NACA 2412 tapered wing, lofted from a 120 mm-chord root section at z = 0 to an 80 mm-chord tip at z = 0.200 m, leading edge unswept (LE at x = 0 in both sections, so zero LE sweep — the quarter-chord line therefore carries the taper's implied 5.7° sweep; the request said "no sweep" without naming a reference line) and no twist (both sections in parallel planes, same orientation). Root sits on the z = 0 wall. Domain: x −0.48 → +1.08 (4 root chords ahead of the LE, 8 behind the TE), y ±0.36 (3 chords each side), z 0 → 0.56 (3 chords above the tip). Fluid = box − wing; all in metres.

**Measured against the request:** root chord 0.11990 at z = 0.0005 (expect 0.11990), 0.10000 at mid-span, 0.08010 at z = 0.1995 — linear taper 120→80 mm; wing z-extent 0 → 0.2000 m span; t/c = 0.1215 at all three stations (NACA 2412's 12.16 % including camber); sectional area coefficient 0.0818 c²; fluid volume 0.628826 m³ in CAD vs 0.628826 m³ in the mesh.

**Patches** named on the faces as selected (each on its own generating plane of the domain, wing = everything else), one STL each in `constant/triSurface`: inlet 0.4032 m², outlet 0.4032 m², farfield 2.8704 m², root 1.12202 m² (box face minus root section), wing 0.041363 m² CAD vs 0.041346 m² snapped (0.04 % loss to snapping).

**Mesh:** blockMesh 39×18×14 background (40 mm) + snappyHexMesh, surface levels 4–5 (1.25 mm at the wall, ~96 cells/chord at the root), feature-edge snapping on the trailing edge and tip. 69 642 cells, checkMesh OK: max non-orthogonality 49.1, max skewness 1.90, max aspect ratio 5.19.

**Not checked / caveats:** no boundary layers were added (`addLayers false`), so there is no y⁺ control; the sweep convention above is my reading, not a measurement; and I did not verify camber line position from the snapped mesh, only from the source profile (2 % at 40 % chord by construction).
